document_check.note: The document is Gallego-Rudolf J, Wiesman AI, Yakoub Y, Zetterberg H, Blennow K, Baillet S, Villeneuve S et al., 'Prediction of mild cognitive impairment progression using time-sensitive multimodal biomarkers', a medRxiv preprint posted 22 September 2025 (doi:10.1101/2025.09.20.25336240) and not peer reviewed. It is a PREVENT-AD analysis (n = 102, 31 progressors) and matches the cited claims: the clinical model is predictive; plasma, Abeta PET and tau PET add to it; hippocampal volume does not; time-varying alpha power adds beyond clinical and plasma markers.

cited_result: Principal: incremental prediction of progression to MCI from nested Cox models. Plasma Abeta42/40 and p-tau217, neocortical Abeta PET and entorhinal tau PET improved on a clinical and genetic model (likelihood ratio tests vs clinical), while hippocampal volume did not. Also cited: the time-varying alpha-power term improving on clinical plus plasma markers (LRT = 5.12, p(FDR) = 0.0237).
tool_reason: The cited result is the added predictive performance of biomarkers within multivariable Cox prognostic models (model comparison by likelihood ratio, AIC and C-index), which is a multivariable prediction-model question.

domains.rationale: The data come from a prospective longitudinal cohort with clear inclusion criteria. Exclusions were technical (dental-implant MEG noise, poor PET, missing plasma) and are unlikely to relate to the outcome, although they reduce the sample (handled under analysis).

signalling.question: 1.1 Were appropriate data sources used?
signalling.quote: We analyzed data from a subset of participants from the PRe-symptomatic EValuation of Experimental or Novel Treatments for Alzheimer’s Disease (PREVENT-AD) cohort, a longitudinal study of cognitively unimpaired older adults with elevated familial risk for sporadic AD

signalling.question: 1.2 Were all inclusions and exclusions of participants appropriate?
signalling.quote: We excluded 19 participants due to high-amplitude MEG noise from ferromagnetic dental implants, one for poor-quality PET data, and two with missing plasma measurements, yielding 102 participants for analysis.

signalling.question: Were inclusion criteria stated?
signalling.quote: Inclusion criteria required a Montreal Cognitive Assessment score ≥ 26 (Nasreddine et al., 2005) and Clinical Dementia Rating of 0

domains.rationale: Predictors were measured with single-site, standardised MEG, PET, MRI and plasma protocols at baseline, before diagnosis. Blinding of the semi-automated processing is not stated, but the measures are largely automated. MRI and plasma samples were the ones 'closest' to baseline (mean offsets 0.84 and 0.91 years), and a sensitivity analysis of plasma timing gave similar results.

signalling.question: 2.1 Were predictors defined and assessed in a similar way for all participants?
signalling.quote: Relative alpha-band (8–12 Hz) power was averaged across six bilateral temporal-lobe regions (entorhinal, fusiform, inferior parietal, lingual, middle temporal, parahippocampal) and used as the MEG biomarker

signalling.question: 2.2 Were predictor assessments made without knowledge of outcome data?
signalling.quote: All were cognitively unimpaired at biomarker collection

signalling.question: 2.3 Are all predictors available at the time the model is intended to be used?
signalling.quote: Biomarkers were not always collected on the same day, introducing modest timing offsets. However, sensitivity analyses using actual acquisition dates of plasma collection—rather than aligning them to MEG/MRI/PET session dates—yielded nearly identical results, supporting robustness.

signalling.question: Were timing offsets reported?
signalling.quote: The scan closest to MEG/PET acquisition was selected (mean interval = 0.84 years; SD = 0.63).

domains.rationale: MCI was determined by a multidisciplinary consensus panel blinded to APOE and all biomarkers, after annual RBANS testing for everyone, over a mean follow-up of 5.9 years. Named diagnostic criteria are not given, but the procedure is standard for the cohort.

signalling.question: 3.1 Was the outcome determined appropriately?
signalling.quote: Decline in at least one domain prompted review by a multidisciplinary consensus panel at the Centre for Studies on Prevention of Alzheimer’s Disease (StoP-AD).

signalling.question: 3.2 Was a pre-specified or standard outcome definition used?
signalling.quote: The panel, blinded to APOE genotype and all biomarker data, determined MCI status, based on longitudinal neuropsychological, clinical, and medical information.

signalling.question: 3.3 Were predictors excluded from the outcome definition?
signalling.quote: The panel, blinded to APOE genotype and all biomarker data

signalling.question: 3.4 Was the outcome defined and determined in a similar way for all participants?
signalling.quote: PREVENT-AD participants complete annual cognitive testing with the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status (RBANS; Randolph et al., 1998)

signalling.question: 3.5 Was the outcome determined without knowledge of predictor information?
signalling.quote: The panel, blinded to APOE genotype and all biomarker data, determined MCI status

signalling.question: 3.6 Was the time interval between predictor assessment and outcome determination appropriate?
signalling.quote: Over a mean follow-up of 5.88 years (SD = 1.64; range = 0.19–7.45), 31 participants progressed to MCI and 71 remained stable.

domains.rationale: With 31 events, the full model (4 clinical plus 6 biomarker terms) and the stepwise model (plus 2 time interactions) have roughly 3 events per parameter. It is a complete-case analysis (22 of 124 excluded). Time-interaction terms were carried forward because they were significant in the same data, and a stepwise AIC selection was used. No calibration is reported. No cross-validation, bootstrap or shrinkage was done, so all performance is apparent. The 'extended samples' contain the main cohort and have no MEG, so they are not independent validation of the alpha-power findings.

signalling.question: 4.1 Were there a reasonable number of participants with the outcome?
signalling.quote: Limitations include the relatively small sample size, reflecting the difficulty of acquiring longitudinal multimodal data in at-risk but asymptomatic individuals, and class imbalance (31 progressors vs. 71 non-progressors).

signalling.question: 4.2 Were continuous and categorical predictors handled appropriately?
signalling.quote: Time-varying associations between the z-scored biomarker values and the predicted log risk scores

signalling.question: 4.3 Were all enrolled participants included in the analysis?
signalling.quote: The main analytic sample comprised 124 participants who underwent Aβ and tau PET imaging and resting-state MEG between 2017 and 2019.

signalling.question: 4.4 Were participants with missing data handled appropriately?
signalling.quote: We excluded 19 participants due to high-amplitude MEG noise from ferromagnetic dental implants, one for poor-quality PET data, and two with missing plasma measurements, yielding 102 participants for analysis.

signalling.question: 4.5 Was selection of predictors based on univariable analysis avoided?
signalling.quote: For time-dependent effects, we added biomarker × time interaction terms to each of the models combining clinical and biomarker information, entering them individually while keeping the rest of the predictors as linear terms.

signalling.question: 4.5 (continued) Was data-driven predictor selection used for the final model?
signalling.quote: A stepwise selection procedure (step, base R) was applied to the full model (all biomarkers + significant time interactions) to identify a parsimonious predictor set.

signalling.question: 4.6 Were complexities in the data (censoring, non-proportional hazards) accounted for appropriately?
signalling.quote: Models were fitted with coxph; proportional hazards assumptions were tested using cox.zph.

signalling.question: 4.7 Were relevant model performance measures evaluated appropriately (including calibration)?
signalling.quote: Model performance was assessed via likelihood ratio tests (LRTs) against the null model (FDR-corrected, n = 7). Pairwise LRTs compared each biomarker model to the clinical model (FDR-corrected, n = 6).

signalling.question: 4.8 Were model overfitting, underfitting and optimism accounted for? (AI-specific: split, held-out test set, apparent vs validated performance)
signalling.quote: While Cox models are robust to moderate class imbalance (Cox, 1972), the sample size precluded the use of cross-validation or more complex machine learning approaches.

signalling.question: Is the replication sample independent of the development sample?
signalling.quote: we also examined three extended PREVENT-AD samples comprising the main analysis cohort plus participants with available plasma or PET biomarkers but no MEG scans.

signalling.question: 4.9 Do predictors and their assigned weights in the final model correspond to the results from the reported multivariable analysis?
signalling.quote: The algorithm selected a final parsimonious model comprising age (log(HR) = 0.32, HR = 1.38, p = 0.1326), hippocampal volume (log(HR) = 0.39, HR = 1.48, p = 0.0661), the time-varying effect of alpha power (log(HR) = 0.01, HR = 1.01, p = 0.0047), neocortical Aβ PET burden (log(HR) = 0.44, HR = 1.55, p = 0.0086), and entorhinal tau PET uptake (log(HR) = 0.60, HR = 1.82, p = 0.0027)

overall_rationale: Participants, predictors and outcome are low risk, but the analysis domain is high. The events-per-parameter ratio is very low, the analysis is complete-case, interaction terms and the stepwise model were selected on the same data, no calibration is reported, and there was no internal or external validation, so the incremental-value estimates are apparent and optimistic. Under PROBAST, any high domain gives an overall high rating.

applicability.rationale: The sample is cognitively unimpaired volunteers with a parental or multiple-sibling history of AD, and the outcome is progression to MCI (not MCI to dementia). This limits transfer to general MCI populations.
The predictors are research-grade MEG (275-channel), HRRT PET and mass-spectrometry and Simoa plasma assays, which are not routinely available.
The outcome is consensus-panel MCI diagnosis, which is relevant to preclinical risk prediction.
